objective_record.compatibility: a legacy suite record (version 2) without the section, a version-4 record without the identity and a version-5 record whose identity is the older shape all still verify, which is what keeps the runs of this experiment written by every earlier writer valid; the current version's writer always emits the section and the identity, so deleting either from a newly written record is reported, and a version-5 record carrying the current shape's wrapper digest is reported too, because no writer of that version emitted one. A record whose configuration has no Tetris agent must not carry the section, because no writer emits one.

identity.covers: the declaring module, every package module its code calls — the frozen geometry and board model it imports and Experiment 002's reachable-set enumeration it reuses — and, since the 63e432f round, the agent wrapper that produces the choices: the module that defines the agent factory, which selects the class, and the class whose _choose hands the objective every state parameter it reads (the board, the current and preview pieces, the level, the lines, the start level, the first-delay countdown, the ruleset and the mode) and executes the placement it returns. The digest of each covered module is the source the interpreter loaded, fixed by the loader that read it and never revised, not a later read of module.__file__ — which is only a path, and the bug the 9799d59e round repairs. The set is discovered from the code rather than hand-listed — the objective's own namespace and the module that defines the factory, from which the class it returns is reached — so a module that stops producing choices drops out of the identity by itself, and neither a helper's change nor a wrapper's can move the objective's values unrecorded. The wrapper imports the objective rather than the other way round, which is why the walk that stopped at the objective's own imports could not reach it
identity.gating: required at version 6, the version the current writer emits, under the shape that covers the wrapper; a version-5 record is compared against the older shape its own writer recorded — the modules the objective's own imports reach — because that is the identity it carries and the retained version-5 records must keep verifying. Optional at version 4 and 2, whose writers recorded no identity, and compared when present
identity.value: one sha256 per package module the objective's choices are computed from, keyed by module name
identity.why: the weights are constants, so a formula change that leaves them alone changes every value the objective computes while the recorded weights still compare equal, and the replayed choices catch it only when the change happens to move one of them. The reviewer's counterexample — the clear term charging a premature clear at twice the declared rate — keeps every weight and is reported by this identity alone; and the wrapper could hand the objective a different state parameter or bypass the objective altogether while the recorded seeds kept exactly their actions, which the identity misses as long as it stops at the objective's own imports — the finding this round repairs, executed as prechange_probe.py objective_wrapper_identity; and the identity is read from each module's path at the moment the writer imports it, so a file edited between a module's own import and the writer's import is recorded though the loaded code chose the inputs — the finding the 9799d59e round repairs, executed as prechange_probe.py loaded_identity

objective_record.place: a top-level suite section beside the frozen heuristic mapping, never a leaf inside an episode or its result; required by a suite that uses the Tetris agent at every version whose writer emits one (4, 5 and 6), optional only at the legacy version 2
objective_record.source: tetris.weights_record(): the declared weights, the well-depth cap and the tie-break rule, plus the objective's source identity
objective_record.verification: verify_run compares the recorded module name, weights and source identity with the current module's under the same exact type-and-key rules it applies to the heuristic mapping, so a suite that uses the Tetris agent cannot verify under a different objective merely because the change preserved its replayed choices; live play, the second path that writes suite records, records the same section for a live Tetris game; the identity's shape is selected from the record's own format_version, so the writer and the verifier enumerate the same closure for the version that wrote the record; the identity the writer records is the loaded code rather than a later read of the tree — the loader that read each module's source fixes its digest — so the writer's claim is the code that ran, and the verifier's tree view reports the record instead of certifying it once a covered file has moved on
objective_record.why: the frozen heuristic mapping is recorded for every suite because every placement agent scores through it, and the Tetris agent's choices come from a second, separately declared objective; before this section existed a suite record was tied to its objective only through the replayed choices, so a changed objective still verified whenever the change happened to preserve them, and before the identity existed a changed formula still verified whenever its weights were unchanged

predeclared_objective.identity_coverage: the capture records the digest of every module the objective's decisions are computed from, the same set the run record's objective.sources identity enumerates, discovered through the runner's one closure walk rather than hand-listed; check-predeclaration requires that mapping to equal the current modules and, when the cited record's version carries one, the identity the run itself wrote, and requires the declaring module's digest to be the identity's entry for it. The capture reads the tree and the writer reads the loaded bytes, and that asymmetry is deliberate: the capture declares the objective as it stands before the run and the check re-reads the tree, while the record names the code that ran. A capture whose tree bytes differ from the record's loaded identity is exactly the mismatch the check reports, so neither can bless a record whose implementation is not the one it names. Before the a14fe1843 round the capture recorded only src/block_stack_ai/tetris.py, so a post-capture change to a helper moved every value the objective computes and was not reported, and before the 9799d59e round the record's own identity was read from each module's path, so an edit landing before the writer imported was certified: both are executed as prechange_probe.py rows
